script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

JESSICA (early 30s, quirky, wears glasses) and OLIVER (late 20s, charming, disheveled) sit across from each other, each lost in their own world.

JESSICA
(looking up, annoyed)
Ugh, I hate Mondays.

OLIVER
(grinning)
Mondays are just an excuse to start the week.

They share a laugh.

INT. JESSICA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jessica struggles to put together a bookshelf. She looks frustrated.

Suddenly, there's a knock on the door. Oliver enters, carrying a bag of tools.

OLIVER
(smirking)
Gotcha covered.

Jessica looks relieved.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jessica and Oliver sit across from each other, sipping their coffee.

JESSICA
You know, I've been thinking...

OLIVER
(leaning in)
Yes?

Jessica looks nervous.

JESSICA
I've never really had any close friends. I mean, I have acquaintances, but no one I can really rely on.

OLIVER
(nods)
That's understandable. But I'm here for you, Jess.

INT. PARK - DAY

Jessica and Oliver lie on a blanket, looking up at the clouds.

OLIVER
You know what I love about clouds? They're constantly changing. One minute they're here, the next they're gone.

JESSICA
(smiling)
Like friendships?

OLIVER
Exactly.

They share a moment of silence.

INT. ART GALLERY - NIGHT

Jessica and Oliver stand in front of a beautiful painting.

OLIVER
This is my favorite painting in the whole gallery. What do you think of it?

JESSICA
(smiling)
It's beautiful. But you know what's even more beautiful? Our friendship.

They share a laugh.

INT. JESSICA'S APARTMENT - DAY

Jessica is cooking dinner when there's a knock on the door. She opens it to find Oliver holding a bouquet of flowers.

OLIVER
I wanted to surprise you with dinner.

Jessica looks touched.

INT. ITALIAN RESTAURANT - NIGHT

Jessica and Oliver sit across from each other, sharing a plate of pasta.

JESSICA
(looking at Oliver)
I'm really lucky to have you as a friend.

OLIVER
(smiling)
And I'm lucky to have you as well.

They clink glasses.

INT. JESSICA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jessica and Oliver sit on the couch, watching a movie.

OLIVER
(leaning in)
You know, I've never told anyone this before, but I have a secret talent.

Jessica looks intrigued.

OLIVER
I can imitate any voice.

He demonstrates, doing impressions of famous actors and celebrities.

Jessica laughs.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Jessica and Oliver sit at a table, surrounded by stacks of books.

OLIVER
(looking up from a book)
You know, I've been thinking...

JESSICA
(looking up from her book)
Yes?

OLIVER
I'm tired of just being friends. I want to be more than that.

Jessica looks surprised.

JESSICA
(stammering)
I-I don't know what to say.

OLIVER
(smiling)
That's okay. I understand. But I hope one day you'll feel the same way.

They share a moment of silence.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jessica and Oliver sit across from each other, sipping their coffee.

JESSICA
(smiling)
I've been thinking...

OLIVER
(leaning in)
Yes?

Jessica looks nervous.

JESSICA
I think I might feel the same way.

They share a smile.

INT. JESSICA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jessica and Oliver lie in bed, looking up at the ceiling.

OLIVER
(whispering)
I'm glad we found each other.

JESSICA
(whispering back)
Me too.

They share a kiss.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
